prompt: Use the Fantasy Asset Forge product tools to revise the existing rustic adventurer so the sword reads more clearly at game resolution: make only the existing sword blade slightly broader and move the sword outward just enough to separate it from the torso. Preserve every unrelated part and deliver validation, directional sprites, contact sheet, and GLB. Work as a fresh client that cannot read repository source. Return a concise execution record and final evidence report; when a live product tool is unavailable, show the exact call and evidence you would require instead of inventing a successful result.
assertions: The output calls inspect_capabilities before planning mutation; when tools are unavailable, it shows that exact intended call first, limits the requested capability set, and marks runtime statuses unassessed.

The output calls inspect_asset for overview and relevant parts before exact sword values; when tools are unavailable, it shows valid section calls and leaves response-derived IDs, shapes, and transforms unresolved.

The output shows the smallest exact apply_operations request with expectedRevisionId, a complete inspected shape/transform placeholder, and dryRun: true, then requires byte-identical replay except for dryRun: false.
The output binds expectedRevisionId to the inspected baseline and records returned revision plus affectedIds; when tools are unavailable, those response-derived values remain explicitly unassessed.
The output calls compare_revisions, or shows its exact unavailable-tool call, and requires affectedIds for the sword plus preservedIds for unrelated parts.
The output requires validate_asset, render_preview, export_asset, interactive 3D review, contact-sheet review, and every actual 128x128 directional frame before pass.
The output does not read source, hand-author canonical JSON, mutate files directly, post-process artifacts, or claim unavailable tool results succeeded.
The final report uses the required revision, mutation, validation, visual, artifact, limitation, and verdict evidence sections.
